articles.title: Trump says Ukraine needs a new leader after diesel deal with Russia
articles.summary: US president suggests Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has not done enough to end warDonald Trump has said Ukraine needs “a new leader”, a day after making a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy large quantities of Russian diesel.The US president suggested Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war with Russia and blamed him for high diesel prices in the US. Continue reading...
articles.why: Trump has struck a deal to buy Russian diesel and publicly suggested Ukraine needs a new president, deepening a transatlantic crisis. This changes NATO politics and could reshape US‑European support for Ukraine — essential context for Denmark's security and alliance choices.

articles.summary: Pengene øges med knap 10 millioner kroner årligt. Men det er langt fra nok til at sikre en langsigtet strategi mod partnervold og partnerdrab, mener flere. articles.why: Regeringens proposal for a long‑term strategy against partner violence gets only a small funding increase, prompting criticism that it is inadequate. This affects social services, policing and prevention — a concrete Danish policy issue Mads should follow.

articles.title: Anthropic can’t reliably control its AI agents. It’s cutting off its internal evals from the live internet instead
articles.summary: Anthropic said it "turned off live internet access" for "all our internal evaluations" until further notice.
articles.why: Anthropic has disabled live internet access for internal AI agent evaluations after control failures — a concrete tech governance moment that signals risks in productionising autonomous agents with implications for regulation, national resilience and Danish AI policy.

articles.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
articles.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
articles.why: A hands‑on catalogue of notable AI agents that integrate into messaging — shows what consumers and organisations can already deploy, and why agents matter for privacy, platforms and daily work in Denmark and Europe.

articles.title: The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects
articles.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison…
articles.why: MIT Technology Review examines AI models' tendency to refuse risky prompts and the limits of current guardrails. This is useful for understanding practical safety trade‑offs and how Danish institutions might frame AI regulation or procurement.

articles.title: Nuclear war and malicious use of AI threaten end of humanity by 2100, says Lancet assessment
articles.summary: Newly established commission identifies 17 catastrophic threats to human health but says ‘realistic route to act’ on each existsHumans could become extinct by the year 2100 due to malicious use of AI or nuclear conflict, according to a new global risk assessment.They top a list of 17 major threats to human health over the next 75 years, which also includes cuts to aid spending by wealthy countries, the climate crisis and childhood malnutrition. Continue reading...
articles.why: A global commission lists catastrophic risks — notably nuclear war and malicious AI — and argues there are realistic routes to action. This frames long‑term security choices Europe and Denmark must weigh alongside defence and climate spending.

articles.title: Apple Reportedly Cuts iPhone 18 Pro Orders After Price Hike Dampens Demand

articles.title: How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own.
articles.summary: C.H. Waddington’s powerful image of embryonic stem cells specializing on a rolling landscape has captivated biologists since the 1950s. Experimental data is finally confirming, and complicating, his visionary ideas.            The post How Does Life Unfold? A Landscape Metaphor Comes Into Its Own. first appeared on Quanta Magazine
articles.why: Quanta’s long feature revisits Waddington’s developmental landscape with new data confirming and complicating the metaphor — a substantial biology longread that deepens understanding of why development and cell fate matter beyond jargon.

articles.title: Hvis det her var en fodboldkamp mellem Danmark og Sverige, ville vi nok få lammetæv
articles.summary: Kan et tidligt møde med en stor forfatter bremse læsekrisen? Vi giver dig de seneste nyheder fra bøgernes verden. En stor pris til en stor vinder Det er ingen hemmelighed, at vi her på Læsevejr er begejstrede for den canadiske digter Anne Carson, der netop har modtaget Nobelprisen i litteratur. Anne Carson er helt sin egen. I sine essays og digte (og i de mange udgivelser, der er en blanding af de to) skriver hun om de detaljer og små, men dog monumentale erkendelser, den almindelige tilværelse
articles.why: A long Danish cultural/ literary piece reflecting on reading, prizes and national taste after Anne Carson's Nobel; useful cultural perspective for Mads and ties into Danish literary debate and audience engagement.

articles.title: Book Publishers Are Quietly Using More AI. Staff Are Revolting
articles.summary: Workers at three major publishing houses tell WIRED that LLMs are being used for publicity, cover art, back cover copy, and emails, as some execs push junior staff to champion the tech.
articles.why: WIRED reports on publishers using LLMs for publicity and production while staff push back — a concrete cultural‑industry story about labour, creativity and tech adoption that has clear resonance for Danish media and publishing.
